questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }

  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

content.text: Plain output style is active. Remember to follow the specific guidelines for this style.

Upstream OrcaSlicer offers 23 interface languages. That count comes from the current upstream `main` branch (fetched today, commit `3bfabc9831`). Only three of the 23 are tied to a specific region. Every other language has a single version with no regional variants.

The language picker in Preferences, in `src/slic3r/GUI/Preferences.cpp`, lists 24 languages in the code. It only shows a language that also has a translation catalog in `localization/i18n/`. Romanian is in the code's list but has no catalog, so people never see it. That leaves these 23:

- **English**: the source language, which also has its own catalog.
- **Three regional variants**:
  - Simplified Chinese (zh_CN)
  - Traditional Chinese (zh_TW)
  - Brazilian Portuguese (pt_BR)
- **Nineteen languages with no region**:
  - Basque
  - Catalan
  - Czech
  - Dutch
  - French
  - German
  - Hungarian
  - Italian
  - Japanese
  - Korean
  - Lithuanian
  - Polish
  - Russian
  - Spanish
  - Swedish
  - Thai
  - Turkish
  - Ukrainian
  - Vietnamese

Chinese has two versions, Simplified and Traditional, and they are separate catalogs. Portuguese exists only as Brazilian Portuguese; there is no European Portuguese. English and Spanish each have a single version with no regional variants.

I checked the catalog folders and the picker's list. I did not open each catalog to see how complete its translation is, so some languages may still have many untranslated strings.

agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md:85:**Violation.** Removing an upstream snapshot label that upstream later localized. Git stops for a human, but the intent-faithful resolution throws the translation away, and nothing at the site says otherwise.
agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md:111:**Mechanism.** The fork follows upstream's release branches, and each release branch splits off upstream's development line on its own. A plain merge picks the common ancestor itself, a development-line commit from before both release branches. Its conflict list is then everything that differs between the two release branches: vendor profiles, translations, CI files, none of it ours. Naming the last release we took as the base limits the merge to the fork's own changes. That gives the same conflicts a replay would hit, resolved once, with no commits rewritten, so branches in progress merge forward without a rebase. Measured on 2026-11-07, going from v2.4.2 to v2.5.0: 22 conflicted files either way, and a branch in progress merged into the trial result with no conflicts.

Its implementation reads and changes the open project through the typed workspace interface. Two adapters, one for OpenAI and one for MCP, only translate that single definition into the format each side expects. The aim of this guide is a tool catalog that stays small, does only what it claims to do, can change safely over time, and is shaped by real printing tasks.     English text so the fallback also reads correctly;

    product, so the untranslated UI switches too.

# translation may move the word ("Куб Orca").

    "Open-source slicing stands on a tradition",
    "OrcaSlicer began in that same spirit",
    "Today, OrcaSlicer is the most widely used",
    "Orca Slicer is based on PrusaSlicer",
)

    return (s.replace(r"\n", "\n").replace(r"\t", "\t").replace(r"\"", '"').replace(r"\\", "\\"))


def parse_po(path):

content.text:
I haven't changed anything yet. Translating the fork into the same 23 languages as upstream (English plus 22 translations) is a large job, and three decisions are yours before I start.

**What's there today.** If someone sets the app to German, upstream's own windows show German. The fork's windows mostly stay English:

- **Native windows** (the menus, the left pane, the Check print dialog, the printer window, and so on): 33 files already mark their text for translation, about 490 distinct strings. About 110 of those happen to match upstream text and already translate. The other 380 never do, because none of these files are listed in `localization/i18n/list.txt`, so their text is never collected. Some text the native code sends to the pages isn't marked at all; I haven't counted that yet.
- **The web pages** (AI chat, Home, Preferences, setup cards, sign-in): about 600 strings written straight into the code in English, with no translation support of any kind.

That comes to about 1,000 to 1,300 strings, each needing 22 translations.

**What I propose (not agreed yet):**

- **Native windows.** Mark the remaining text and keep the fork's translations in its own catalog files. The build already runs a script, `Brand/brand_catalogs.py`, that builds the translation files the app loads. It would merge the fork's catalogs in too. Upstream's translation files stay untouched, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release brings no translation conflicts.
- **Web pages.** Add Lingui, an established React translation library that pulls text out of the page code into the same `.po` file format. The app tells each page its language when the page opens.
- **AI-facing text stays English.** That covers prompts, skills and tool descriptions; the existing `wording.test.ts` guard already covers that text. The AI keeps replying in whatever language the person writes in.
- **Doing the translation.** One subagent per language, following the repo's translation rules: every entry gets a `# AI Translated` comment, entries I'm unsure of get `# Needs human review`, and every catalog must pass a `msgfmt` check. Then I'd run the app in German and in Japanese and screenshot the main screens to check the result.

**Decision needed: may the 22 languages ship as machine translations with no native-speaker review?** The project has no translators lined up. Shipping them means people will sometimes see awkward wording until someone reports it. Holding each language until a native speaker checks it could take months. A middle path is to ship a few languages now and the rest later. I'd ship all 22, marked as AI-translated. Is that acceptable?

**Decision needed: should the in-app guide be translated too?** The guide is the pages in `docs/guide/`: 7 pages with screenshots. The app shows it in a window, and the same pages also build the AI's guide skill. Translating it roughly doubles the work. The screenshots would still show English, and every release's guide check would have to cover 23 versions. I'd keep the guide English for now and translate it separately later. Do you agree?

**Decision needed: should this start now, or wait for the uncommitted work in the main checkout?** The main checkout has about 60 changed files from the error-handling work. Marking text touches many of the same files, such as `App.tsx`, `Preferences.tsx`, `SetupCard.tsx` and about 40 native files. If I start now in my own worktree, whoever lands second resolves the conflicts. If I wait, nothing conflicts, but nothing starts until that work is committed. I'd wait for that work to land, and meanwhile build only the plumbing, which touches different files. Should I do that?

---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: subagent-worktrees-create-manually
description: "Agent tool isolation:\"worktree\" cut worktrees from a stale base and SendMessage was disabled; create worktrees by hand on the intended commit and pass absolute paths"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 598f26fe-b466-4336-928e-14d10d45e1f7
  modified: 2026-09-08T16:33:59.964Z
---

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. **Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

# JusPrin Agent UI

The local React/TypeScript application that renders the Agent conversation
pane inside `wxWebView`. It talks to OrcaSlicer exclusively through the
versioned `jusprin-agent-bridge` JSON protocol whose shared source of truth is
`resources/jusprin/agent/protocol.json`; the native side lives in
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/`.

The page renders native state and submits typed requests. It never owns an
editable copy of the project or conversation: the native `AgentHost` is
authoritative, and every reload re-runs the handshake and reconstructs the
page from the host's `state` message.

## Building

CMake builds this page whenever an input changes (`npm ci` from the lockfile, then `npm run build`). The output is `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html`; it is generated, not committed. Node/npm is required unless you configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply that file yourself.

```bash
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target jusprin_web
```

The bundle must stay a single self-contained file (`vite-plugin-singlefile`):
WKWebView does not reliably load `file:` subresources.

To point the running app at a Vite dev server instead of the packaged file (hot
module reload):

```bash
cd src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI && npm run dev
JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://localhost:5173 ./build/arm64/src/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer
```

Adjust the binary path for your build tree and platform. The environment
variable is read once at construction; there is no settings UI for it.

## Testing

```bash
npm test        # vitest: protocol, bridge client, reducer, and DOM interaction tests
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Collect JusPrin's own interface text into its translation catalogs.

JusPrin keeps its translations apart from OrcaSlicer's, so taking a new
OrcaSlicer release never conflicts in a catalog:

  * native/JusPrin.pot and native/<lang>.po hold the text the native windows
    mark with _L, _u8L, L, _L_CONTEXT and _L_PLURAL under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin.
    Text OrcaSlicer's own template already has is left out: its translations
    come from upstream. Brand/brand_catalogs.py merges these into the catalog
    the app loads.
  * pages/<lang>.po hold the text of the AI and Home pages, marked with the
    Lingui macros (t, Trans, Plural). Lingui's own extractor writes them.

Run it after marking or changing text, then translate the new entries:

    python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py

Needs GNU gettext (xgettext, msgmerge, msgcat, msgcomm) and the pages'
node_modules (npm ci in AgentUI).
"""

import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
JUSPRIN = HERE.parent
ROOT = JUSPRIN.parents[3]
UPSTREAM_I18N = ROOT / "localization" / "i18n"
NATIVE = HERE / "native"
PAGES = HERE / "pages"

# The same keywords upstream's scripts/run_gettext.sh passes.
XGETTEXT_KEYWORDS = [
    "--keyword=L", "--keyword=_L", "--keyword=_u8L",
    "--keyword=L_CONTEXT:1,2c", "--keyword=_L_CONTEXT:1,2c", "--keyword=_u8L_CONTEXT:1,2c",
    "--keyword=_L_PLURAL:1,2",
]
# Test doubles and the page projects are not native interface text.
SKIP_DIRS = {"Testing", "AgentUI", "HomeUI", "WebShared", "node_modules", "Localization"}

DATE = re.compile(r'^"POT-Creation-Date: .*\\n"\n', re.M)


def languages():
    data = json.loads((HERE / "languages.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return [l["code"] for l in data["languages"] if l["code"] != data["source"]]


def run(*args, **kw):
    subprocess.run(list(args), check=True, **kw)


def keep_if_only_date_changed(path, before):
    """Leave a file as it was when only its creation date moved."""
    if before is not None and path.exists() and DATE.sub("", path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) == DATE.sub("", before):
        path.write_text(before, encoding="utf-8")


def native_sources():
    files = []
    for f in sorted(JUSPRIN.rglob("*")):
        if f.suffix in (".cpp", ".hpp") and not SKIP_DIRS.intersection(f.relative_to(JUSPRIN).parts):
            files.append(str(f.relative_to(ROOT)))
    return files


def upstream_header_line(lang, name):
    po = UPSTREAM_I18N / lang / f"OrcaSlicer_{lang}.po"
    m = re.search(rf'^"{name}: (.*)\\n"$', po.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), re.M)
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def update_native():
    NATIVE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    pot = NATIVE / "JusPrin.pot"
    before = pot.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if pot.exists() else None
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        tmp = Path(tmp)
        listing = tmp / "files.txt"
        listing.write_text("\n".join(native_sources()) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        everything = tmp / "all.pot"
        run("xgettext", *XGETTEXT_KEYWORDS, "--add-comments=TRN", "--from-code=UTF-8", "--no-location",
            "--boost", "--no-wrap", "--package-name=JusPrin", "-f", str(listing), "-o", str(everything), cwd=ROOT)
        # Entries OrcaSlicer's template also has keep upstream's translations.
        shared = tmp / "shared.pot"
        run("msgcomm", "--more-than=1", "--no-wrap", "-o", str(shared), str(everything),
            str(UPSTREAM_I18N / "OrcaSlicer.pot"))
        if shared.exists():
            run("msgcat", "--unique", "--no-wrap", "-o", str(pot), str(everything), str(shared))
        else:
            shutil.copy(everything, pot)
    text = pot.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("charset=CHARSET", "charset=UTF-8")
    pot.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    keep_if_only_date_changed(pot, before)

    for lang in languages():
        po = NATIVE / f"{lang}.po"
        before = po.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if po.exists() else None
        if po.exists():
            run("msgmerge", "--quiet", "-N", "--no-wrap", "--previous", "-U", "--backup=none", str(po), str(pot))
        else:
            header = pot.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            plural = upstream_header_line(lang, "Plural-Forms") or "nplurals=2; plural=(n != 1);"
            header = header.replace('"Language: \\n"', f'"Language: {lang}\\n"')
            header = re.sub(r'"Plural-Forms: .*\\n"', f'"Plural-Forms: {plural}\\\\n"', header)
            header = header.replace("#, fuzzy\nmsgid \"\"", "msgid \"\"", 1)
            po.write_text(header, encoding="utf-8")
        keep_if_only_date_changed(po, before)


def update_pages():
    before = {p: p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") for p in PAGES.glob("*.po")}
    npx = shutil.which("npx") or shutil.which("npx.cmd")
    if npx is None:
        sys.exit("update_catalogs: npx not found; the page catalogs need Node")
    run(npx, "lingui", "extract", "--clean", cwd=JUSPRIN / "AgentUI")
    for path, text in before.items():
        keep_if_only_date_changed(path, text)


def main():
    for tool in ("xgettext", "msgmerge", "msgcat", "msgcomm"):
        if shutil.which(tool) is None:
            sys.exit(f"update_catalogs: {tool} not found; install GNU gettext")
    update_native()
    update_pages()
    print("update_catalogs: native/JusPrin.pot, native/<lang>.po and pages/<lang>.po are up to date")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Collect JusPrin's own interface text into its translation catalogs.

JusPrin keeps its translations apart from OrcaSlicer's, so taking a new
OrcaSlicer release never conflicts in a catalog:

  * native/JusPrin.pot and native/<lang>.po hold the text the native windows
    mark with _L, _u8L, L, _L_CONTEXT and _L_PLURAL under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin.
    Text OrcaSlicer's own template already has is left out: its translations
    come from upstream. Brand/brand_catalogs.py merges these into the catalog
    the app loads.
  * pages/<lang>.po hold the text of the AI and Home pages, marked with the
    Lingui macros (t, Trans, Plural). Lingui's own extractor writes them.

Run it after marking or changing text, then translate the new entries:

    python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py

Needs GNU gettext (xgettext, msgmerge, msgcat, msgcomm) and the pages'
node_modules (npm ci in AgentUI).
"""

import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
JUSPRIN = HERE.parent
ROOT = JUSPRIN.parents[3]
UPSTREAM_I18N = ROOT / "localization" / "i18n"
NATIVE = HERE / "native"
PAGES = HERE / "pages"

# The same keywords upstream's scripts/run_gettext.sh passes.
XGETTEXT_KEYWORDS = [
    "--keyword=L", "--keyword=_L", "--keyword=_u8L",
    "--keyword=L_CONTEXT:1,2c", "--keyword=_L_CONTEXT:1,2c", "--keyword=_u8L_CONTEXT:1,2c",
    "--keyword=_L_PLURAL:1,2",
]
# Test doubles and the page projects are not native interface text.
SKIP_DIRS = {"Testing", "AgentUI", "HomeUI", "WebShared", "node_modules", "Localization"}

DATE = re.compile(r'^"POT-Creation-Date: .*\\n"\n', re.M)


def languages():
    data = json.loads((HERE / "languages.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return [l["code"] for l in data["languages"] if l["code"] != data["source"]]


def run(*args, **kw):
    subprocess.run(list(args), check=True, **kw)


def keep_if_only_date_changed(path, before):
    """Leave a file as it was when only its creation date moved."""
    if before is not None and path.exists() and DATE.sub("", path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) == DATE.sub("", before):
        path.write_text(before, encoding="utf-8")


def native_sources():
    files = []
    for f in sorted(JUSPRIN.rglob("*")):
        if f.suffix in (".cpp", ".hpp") and not SKIP_DIRS.intersection(f.relative_to(JUSPRIN).parts):
            files.append(str(f.relative_to(ROOT)))
    return files


def upstream_header_line(lang, name):
    po = UPSTREAM_I18N / lang / f"OrcaSlicer_{lang}.po"
    m = re.search(rf'^"{name}: (.*)\\n"$', po.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), re.M)
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def update_native():
    NATIVE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    pot = NATIVE / "JusPrin.pot"
    before = pot.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if pot.exists() else None
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        tmp = Path(tmp)
        listing = tmp / "files.txt"
        listing.write_text("\n".join(native_sources()) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        everything = tmp / "all.pot"
        run("xgettext", *XGETTEXT_KEYWORDS, "--add-comments=TRN", "--from-code=UTF-8", "--no-location",
            "--boost", "--no-wrap", "--package-name=JusPrin", "-f", str(listing), "-o", str(everything), cwd=ROOT)
        # Entries OrcaSlicer's template also has keep upstream's translations.
        shared = tmp / "shared.pot"
        run("msgcomm", "--more-than=1", "--no-wrap", "-o", str(shared), str(everything),
            str(UPSTREAM_I18N / "OrcaSlicer.pot"))
        if shared.exists():
            run("msgcat", "--unique", "--no-wrap", "-o", str(pot), str(everything), str(shared))
        else:
            shutil.copy(everything, pot)
    text = pot.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("charset=CHARSET", "charset=UTF-8")
    pot.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    keep_if_only_date_changed(pot, before)

    for lang in languages():
        po = NATIVE / f"{lang}.po"
        before = po.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if po.exists() else None
        if po.exists():
            run("msgmerge", "--quiet", "-N", "--no-wrap", "--previous", "-U", "--backup=none", str(po), str(pot))
        else:
            header = pot.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            plural = upstream_header_line(lang, "Plural-Forms") or "nplurals=2; plural=(n != 1);"
            header = header.replace('"Language: \\n"', f'"Language: {lang}\\n"')
            header = re.sub(r'"Plural-Forms: .*\\n"', f'"Plural-Forms: {plural}\\\\n"', header)
            header = header.replace("#, fuzzy\nmsgid \"\"", "msgid \"\"", 1)
            po.write_text(header, encoding="utf-8")
        keep_if_only_date_changed(po, before)


def update_pages():
    before = {p: p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") for p in PAGES.glob("*.po")}
    npx = shutil.which("npx") or shutil.which("npx.cmd")
    if npx is None:
        sys.exit("update_catalogs: npx not found; the page catalogs need Node")
    run(npx, "lingui", "extract", "--clean", cwd=JUSPRIN / "AgentUI")
    for path, text in before.items():
        keep_if_only_date_changed(path, text)


def main():
    for tool in ("xgettext", "msgmerge", "msgcat", "msgcomm"):
        if shutil.which(tool) is None:
            sys.exit(f"update_catalogs: {tool} not found; install GNU gettext")
    update_native()
    update_pages()
    print("update_catalogs: native/JusPrin.pot, native/<lang>.po and pages/<lang>.po are up to date")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# JusPrin's translations JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for (`languages.json`). OrcaSlicer's own windows translate through upstream's catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never conflicts in a translation file: | Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL` | `native/.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n//.mo`, the catalog the app loads | | The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) | Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of `native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used. ## Updating the catalogs After marking or changing text: ```bash python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py ``` It runs `xgettext` over the native sources and Lingui's extractor over the pages, then merges the new entries into every language. Translate each new entry in every `.po`, following the editing rules in the repository's `AGENTS.md` (Localization & translations): keep every placeholder and line break, give each plural form its own inflection, and mark machine translations `# AI Translated`, adding `# Needs human review: ` where the meaning or the wording is uncertain. `AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts` fails while any entry is untranslated or a translation loses a placeholder. The page catalogs use ICU placeholders: `{0}`, `{name}`, numbered tags like `<0>…` for elements inside a `Trans`, and `{count, plural, one {# printer} other {# printers}}` for counts. Keep the placeholder and tag names; translate the words, including the words inside a plural's branches, and give the plural the categories the language uses (`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`). ## Marking text Mark every string a person reads: labels, buttons, headings, menu items, tooltips, `aria-label`s, placeholders, empty states, confirmation and error text. Do not change the English: marking must leave the source text exactly as it was. Leave these in English, unmarked: - **Text the AI model reads**: prompts, skills, tool descriptions and tool results, the project and printer instructions, anything that goes into a request to a model. The model speaks the person's language on its own, and `wording.test.ts` guards that text. When the same string is shown to the person and also sent to the model, translate it only where it is shown. - Identifiers and values the code compares, protocol fields, CSS classes, test ids, file names, URLs, setting keys, G-code. - Log lines and the text of error reports (`report_unexpected`, `report_error`): they are read by developers. - Names: JusPrin, OrcaSlicer, Bambu Lab, printer and filament model names. ### In the pages ```tsx import { t, plural } from '@lingui/core/macro'; import { Trans } from '@lingui/react/macro';

Takes effect when {app} restarts. Your project is saved first.

const label = plural(count, { one: '# printer', other: '# printers' }); const title = t({ message: 'Back', context: 'navigation' }); // a word with several meanings const hint = t({ message: 'Fit', comment: 'Verb: scale the model to the plate' }); // a note for translators ``` - One message per sentence. Never build a sentence from translated pieces, and never splice a translated word into another sentence: use a placeholder, or a `Trans` with the element inside it. - A count needs `plural` / `Plural`, not "printer(s)". - Put only plain variables in placeholders (`{name}`, not `{a.b.c}`): the translator sees the variable's name. Pull an expression into a well-named local first. - The language is chosen before the first render and never changes while a page runs, so `t` works anywhere, including at a module's top level and in plain `.ts` files. `Trans` and `useLingui` from the macros need no provider (see `i18n.tsx`). - Tests run in English, so a test that finds text by its English words keeps working. ### In the native code - `_L("…")` gives a `wxString` for a window; `_u8L("…")` gives UTF-8 for JSON sent to a page. - Translate when the text is used, never in a static initializer, which runs before the language is loaded. Mark such a table with `L("…")` and call `_L`/`_u8L` on the entry where it is shown. - Use `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)` rather than concatenation, and `_L_PLURAL` for counts; `// TRN` above a string tells the translator what it means. - Every file that marks text is extracted: `update_catalogs.py` reads every `.cpp` and `.hpp` under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin` except `Testing/`. Do not add JusPrin files to `localization/i18n/list.txt`.

<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>I marked the remaining person-facing text in Home, PrinterSetup and Printers and fixed the rule breaks I found. Preferences, Updates, V1Import and Startup needed no changes. HEAD was d8b891ba80. Nothing is committed and no .po file was touched.

**Decision needed.** While I worked, another helper added `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/Translate.hpp`: `L()` plus a global `translated()` that the app installs at startup. I had already built my own hook for the same job. The printer form's GUI-free files can't use `_L`, because the agent and profile test binaries build them without wx. My hook is a small `Wording` callback that `IPrinterBackend::wording()` returns; the Orca backend translates through it and test backends keep English. The two do the same thing, but `Translate.hpp` has no plural, and the "Made for …" phrase needs one. You could keep both (costs a second mechanism), or add a plural to `Translate.hpp` and switch my files over (about a dozen mechanical edits, which I couldn't make because that file isn't mine). I'd add the plural and switch. Which do you want?

**Files changed** (all under `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/localize-fork/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`):
- `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp`, `Home/OrcaImporter.cpp`
- `PrinterSetup/PrinterBackend.hpp`, `OrcaPrinterBackend.hpp`, `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp`, `PrinterConversation.cpp`, `SetupOptionsLoader.hpp`, `SetupOptionsLoader.cpp`, `PrinterPanel.cpp`
- `Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp`, `Printers/NamedPrinters.hpp`

**Newly marked: about 13 strings.**
- Home printer cards: the nozzle size, "%g mm".
- Home project cards: the short date pattern, with and without the year.
- The "Photos" label in the report photo picker.
- The printer form's four error messages and its profile-read error.
- The "Made for …" phrases, with a plural for the count.
- The form's plate names now go through translation where they are shown. OrcaSlicer's catalogs already have them.

**Existing marks fixed: about 17.**
- "Klipper stopped:" was joined to the message with `+`. It is now one string with a placeholder.
- Five strings had two `%s` placeholders, which translators can't reorder. They now use `%1%`/`%2%`, and the other project-status strings were moved to the same form.
- "Draft", "Sent" and "Printed" now have a "project status" context. Upstream's plain "Draft" means something else.
- "Back" now uses upstream's "Navigation" context.
- Four messages that only the printer chat's model reads were translated by mistake: in `link_named_printer`, `change_named_printer_nozzle` and `configure_named_printer_host`. They are English again.

**One English change.** When a filament is made for exactly three printers, the form now says "and 1 other printer" instead of "1 other printers". The plural form makes that unavoidable. Tell me if you want the old wording kept.

**Left in English on purpose:**
- Everything in PrinterSetup the model reads: tool results, notes, connection reports, the backend's connect and host-test messages. The build volume in the printer catalogue also goes only to the model.
- Log lines, thrown errors, and the preferences and Home protocol errors (`hello_reject`). Our own code is on both ends, and the page doesn't show them.
- Identifiers: window names, settings keys, status ids, wildcard patterns.
- Names: brands, AMS, Klipper, OctoPrint, the languages' own names, and the "Orca copy" / "JusPrin 1 copy" suffixes, which become part of saved preset names.
- The defaults in `HomeBackend.hpp` ("Connection is unavailable."), which the app always replaces.

**Not sure about these:**
- `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp` decides a project is untitled by comparing its saved name with `_L("Untitled")`. That is behaviour chosen by translated text, and it breaks after a language switch. `ProjectAutosave.cpp` and `AppMenus.cpp` do the same, and both are outside my files, so I left it.
- `remove_named_printer` messages are shown on Home and also sent to the model by the chat's Undo. I kept them translated.
- The filament chat's opening greeting in `PrinterPanel.cpp` is shown and also becomes the model's own history. I left it English.
- The chat's tool activity titles ("Checking <address>", "Waiting for the access code for …") are saved in the project and shown. I left them English to match the rest of the tool titles in `Agent/`; I don't know if they reach the model.

**How I checked it compiles.** The `compile_commands.json` in `build/arm64` holds only 24 files, so I generated the full command list with `ninja -t compdb`. I then ran `-fsyntax-only` one file at a time against the worktree sources, with no precompiled header. All six passed:
- `PrinterConversation.cpp` and `SetupOptionsLoader.cpp`, each in its GUI-free test build.
- `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp`, `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp`, `OrcaImporter.cpp` and `NamedPrinters.cpp` in the GUI build.

I reviewed `PrinterPanel.cpp` without compiling it; the only change there is the context on "Back". Nothing was linked or run.</result>

HomeUI's suite also passes (162 tests), since Home draws the sign-in form. I touched no tests, catalogs or other files, and committed nothing.

To check the English, I rendered the old and new versions of each component side by side, over a few hundred combinations of their inputs, and compared the HTML. That throwaway test lives only in the scratchpad, at `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth--claude-spares-spare-y6RR11/cf003aa0-b151-445c-8bb1-ddda0e13feaf/scratchpad/cmp/all.cmp.test.tsx`. **Files changed** (all under `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/localize-fork/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/`): `components/Preferences.tsx`, `PreferencesApp.tsx`, `components/AgentConnection.tsx`, `components/SignInDoor.tsx`, `components/SetupLocalTool.tsx`, `components/CodeField.tsx`, `components/AllSettings.tsx`, `components/ChangeRows.tsx`.

**Sentences I rebuilt instead of wrapping:**
- **Fallback words spliced into a sentence.** For example, "this account", "This tool", "the settings file" and "the AI tool". Each sentence is now two whole messages, one with the name and one without.
- **"Signed in as {email}" joined to "· AI unavailable".** This is now one message.
- **The key-check error.** It glued the host's message to "Nothing was saved." It is now one message with a placeholder.
- **The Language search in Preferences.** "Find a {label}" lowercased the label inside the sentence. The caller now passes the whole "Find a language" and "No language matches…" text.
- **All settings.** Its own `plural()` helper is replaced by Lingui `plural`. The region and object summaries ("…except in 2 regions: … and …") are now whole plural messages, and "a and b" lists are joined through a "{list} and {name}" message.
- **Kinds of customization and page names.** Kind names ("Support blocker" and the rest) and the group headings ("Quality", "Support"…) are translated where they are shown. The English values the code compares stay as they are.

**Deliberately left in English:**
- **Names:** BYOAI, JusPrin, the provider names Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenRouter, and the "Windows" tag.
- **Values that arrive from the host:** setting labels, page and group names, values, preset and object names, plan name and price line, the server's warning and error text, tool names, subtitles and commands, and change-log labels and locations. One exception: a preset switch's location is one of the words printer, filament or process, so those three are translated.
- **Identifiers and compared values:** `PROCESS_PAGES`, override kinds, section ids, key prefixes such as `sk-ant-`.
- **Number-and-name text and separators:** "1 · PLA", "{n} {volume name}", the " · " and ", " joins, and "—".
- **The `you@example.com` placeholder.**
- **The nav row's `aria-label`.** It joins the section name and its hint with a comma; both halves are already translated.

None of these strings reach the model: the native side words what the model reads.

**Things I was unsure about:**
- **Two places still insert one translated phrase into another message:**
  - "Up to date · checked {checked}" receives a phrase like "2 hours ago".
  - The change log's "{who}, in {preset}" receives "you", "AI" or a tool's name.

  I gave both a note for translators. Writing out every combination would mean about ten messages for the first, and it would break the existing `checkedAgo` test.
